## 1. Introduction

Step 1 (`01_merge`) produced one table with a consistent structure, but the values inside it have not been checked yet. During exploration (`00_data_exploration`), we saw malformed values such as `no express)ion`, `Early adul+t` and `Fan(1`, missing values in many fields, and duplicated analysis IDs.

This step makes every value follow the IMPC Standard Operating Procedure (SOP). The checks follow the order of the module's five data-quality principles: **relevant**, **complete**, **consistent**, **free from errors** and **unique**. Values are only corrected when the correct value can be worked out from the data or a reference file; otherwise they are set to `NA`. Every change is counted and written to a log.

| Input | Output |
|----|----|
| `merged_raw_data.csv` (+ disease and homology files as gene-symbol references) | `cleaned_data.csv`, `cleaned_data_log.csv` |

## 2. Setup

We defined the input and output files, a function that records every change in the log, and the allowed values copied from the SOP, so every check uses the same reference.

```{r}
#| label: s02-setup
args          <- commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)
in_file       <- if (length(args) >= 1) args[1] else "merged_raw_data.csv"
out_file      <- if (length(args) >= 2) args[2] else "cleaned_data.csv"
disease_file  <- if (length(args) >= 3) args[3] else "reference_files/Disease_information.txt"
homology_file <- if (length(args) >= 4) args[4] else "reference_files/bespokeTask_hml.txt"
log_file      <- sub("\\.csv$", "_log.csv", out_file)

change_log <- data.frame(step = character(), column = character(),
                         rows_affected = integer(), detail = character(),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

log_step <- function(step, column, n, detail) {
  change_log[nrow(change_log) + 1, ] <<- list(step, column, as.integer(n), detail)
  message(sprintf("[%s] %-22s %6d rows  %s", step, column, as.integer(n), detail))
}

# Number of entries that differ between two versions of a column (NA-aware)
n_changed <- function(old, new) {
  sum(xor(is.na(old), is.na(new)) | (!is.na(old) & !is.na(new) & old != new))
}

# Most frequent value (ties -> first in sorted order, so results are reproducible)
mode_of <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return(NA_character_)
  tab <- table(x)
  names(tab)[which.max(tab)]
}

# SOP allowed values (IMPC_SOP_2026.csv)
sop_strains <- c("B6Brd;B6Dnk;B6N-Tyr<c-Brd>", "C57BL/6Brd-Tyr<c-Brd>", "C57BL/6Dnk",
                 "C57BL/6JTyr;C57BL/6N", "C57BL/6N", "C57BL/6NCrl", "C57BL/6NJ",
                 "C57BL/6NTac", "C57BL/6NTacDen")
sop_stages  <- c("E9.5", "E12.5", "E15.5", "E18.5",
                 "Early adult", "Middle aged adult", "Late adult")
sop_lacz    <- c("No data", "ambiguous", "expression", "imageOnly",
                 "no expression", "tissue not available")
```

## 3. Read the Merged Data

Everything is read as text, so R does not silently change any values (for example, turning IDs into numbers). An untouched copy, `raw`, is kept for before-and-after comparisons.

```{r}
#| label: s02-read
data <- read.csv(in_file, colClasses = "character", na.strings = character(0),
                 check.names = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
raw  <- data                                   # Untouched copy for comparisons
message(sprintf("Read %s: %d rows x %d columns", in_file, nrow(data), ncol(data)))
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-read
# First rows before cleaning
head(data[, 1:8])
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r nrow(raw)` rows and `r ncol(raw)` columns were read from `merged_raw_data.csv`, matching the output of Step 1.
:::

## 4. Relevant: Required Fields

Before cleaning, we checked that every field required by the SOP is present. If one is missing, the script stops rather than producing an incomplete table.

```{r}
#| label: s02-relevant
lacz_cols <- grep("^lacz_", names(data), value = TRUE)
sop_cols  <- c("analysis_id", "gene_accession_id", "gene_symbol", "strain_name",
               "mouse_life_stage", "parameter_id", "parameter_name", "pvalue",
               "allele_symbol")
missing_cols <- setdiff(sop_cols, names(data))
if (length(missing_cols)) stop("Missing SOP columns: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "))
log_step("1 relevant", "all", nrow(data),
         sprintf("all %d SOP fields present, plus %d lacz_* tissues", length(sop_cols), length(lacz_cols)))

data_cols <- setdiff(names(data), "source_file")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
All `r length(sop_cols)` SOP fields are present, plus `r length(lacz_cols)` `lacz_*` tissue fields.
:::

## 5. Complete: One Meaning for "Missing"

Missing values can be written in many ways (a blank, `"N/A"`, `"NULL"` and so on). We first removed spaces at the start and end of every value, then converted all placeholder text to a real `NA`, so "missing" always means one thing.

```{r}
#| label: s02-complete
for (col in data_cols) {
  old <- data[[col]]
  data[[col]] <- trimws(data[[col]])
  n <- n_changed(old, data[[col]])
  if (n) log_step("2 complete", col, n, "leading/trailing whitespace removed")
}

na_tokens <- c("", "NA", "N/A", "NULL", "NaN", "na", "null")
for (col in data_cols) {
  hit <- !is.na(data[[col]]) & data[[col]] %in% na_tokens
  if (any(hit)) {
    data[[col]][hit] <- NA
    log_step("2 complete", col, sum(hit), "placeholder text ('NA', '' ...) converted to real NA")
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-complete
# Changes made in this section
change_log[change_log$step == "2 complete", ]
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
The table shows which columns contained extra spaces or placeholder text, and how many values were affected. After this step, every missing value is stored as `NA`.
:::

## 6. Consistent: Values in the SOP Format

Each field was then brought into the format the SOP requires. Fields are handled one at a time below.

### 6.1 Analysis and Gene IDs

Broken or missing `analysis_id`s are restored from the file name, which still holds the correct ID. `gene_accession_id` is rebuilt as `MGI:<digits>` (for example, `:2142346` becomes `MGI:2142346`); IDs that cannot be repaired become `NA`. This ID is the key that links to the gene and disease tables in Step 3.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-ids
## 3a analysis_id: 'an' + 10 digits (SOP remark: 12 characters; its min/max of 15 is an SOP error)
old <- data$analysis_id
id_ok   <- !is.na(data$analysis_id) & grepl("^an[0-9]{10}$", data$analysis_id)
from_fn <- sub("(_[0-9]+)?\\.csv$", "", data$source_file)
fix     <- !id_ok & grepl("^an[0-9]{10}$", from_fn)
data$analysis_id[fix] <- from_fn[fix]
if (any(fix)) log_step("3 consistent", "analysis_id", sum(fix), "invalid/missing ID restored from source filename")

## 3b gene_accession_id: MGI:<digits>
old <- data$gene_accession_id
x <- toupper(gsub("\\s", "", data$gene_accession_id))
x <- sub("^(MGI)?:?([0-9]+)$", "MGI:\\2", x)
data$gene_accession_id <- x
n <- n_changed(old, x)
if (n) log_step("3 consistent", "gene_accession_id", n, "repaired to MGI:<digits> (e.g. ':2142346' -> 'MGI:2142346')")
bad <- !is.na(x) & !grepl("^MGI:[0-9]+$", x)
if (any(bad)) { data$gene_accession_id[bad] <- NA
log_step("3 consistent", "gene_accession_id", sum(bad), "unrepairable MGI ID set to NA") }
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r sum(fix)` analysis IDs were restored from their file names. This also settles the question raised in exploration: the real IDs have 12 characters (`an` + 10 digits), so the SOP's minimum and maximum length of 15 is an error in the SOP.
:::

### 6.2 Gene Symbols

Gene symbols contained noise such as `Db^n1` and `MYBL2`. The MGI ID decides which rows belong to the same gene, and each gene is given one symbol. Candidates come from both `gene_symbol` and the start of `allele_symbol`; a symbol confirmed by the disease or homology reference files is preferred, otherwise the most frequent one is used.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-gene-symbol
## 3c gene_symbol: ONE official symbol per MGI ID
# Noise was injected into symbols (Db^n1, Aldo_c, MYBL2). The MGI ID is the stable key,
# so every row of a gene gets the same symbol. Candidates come from gene_symbol AND the
# allele prefix (Mybl2<tm1b...>) after removing illegal characters. The candidate that is
# an official symbol in the Disease Ontology / Ensembl reference files is preferred;
# otherwise the most frequent candidate is used.
clean_sym <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9.-]", "", x)
  x <- gsub("^[.-]+|[.-]+$", "", x)
  x[!is.na(x) & x == ""] <- NA
  x
}
ref_symbols <- character(0)
if (file.exists(disease_file)) {
  dis <- read.delim(disease_file, header = FALSE, comment.char = "#", quote = "",
                    colClasses = "character")
  ref_symbols <- c(ref_symbols, dis[[7]])           # Column 7 = mouse gene symbol
}
if (file.exists(homology_file)) {
  hom <- read.delim(homology_file, quote = "", colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE)
  ref_symbols <- c(ref_symbols, hom[["Gene name"]])
}
ref_symbols <- unique(ref_symbols[nzchar(ref_symbols)])
if (!length(ref_symbols)) warning("No reference symbol files found in reference_files/ - using majority vote only")

cand <- data.frame(mgi = rep(data$gene_accession_id, 2),
                   s   = c(clean_sym(data$gene_symbol),
                           clean_sym(sub("<.*$", "", data$allele_symbol))),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cand <- cand[!is.na(cand$mgi) & !is.na(cand$s), ]

pick_symbol <- function(s) {
  tab <- sort(table(s), decreasing = TRUE)
  in_ref <- names(tab)[names(tab) %in% ref_symbols]
  if (length(in_ref)) return(in_ref[1])
  best <- names(tab)[1]
  # SOP: title format. Upper-case-only names (MUC5AC) -> Muc5ac, but keep
  # accession-style symbols such as AI837181 that are officially upper case.
  if (grepl("^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+$", best) && !grepl("[0-9]{5,}", best))
    best <- paste0(substr(best, 1, 1), tolower(substring(best, 2)))
  best
}
canon_symbol <- tapply(cand$s, cand$mgi, pick_symbol)
n_ref <- sum(canon_symbol %in% ref_symbols)

old <- data$gene_symbol
data$gene_symbol <- unname(canon_symbol[data$gene_accession_id])
log_step("3 consistent", "gene_symbol", n_changed(old, data$gene_symbol),
         sprintf("one symbol per MGI ID (%d of %d genes confirmed by reference files)",
                 n_ref, length(canon_symbol)))
multi <- tapply(data$gene_accession_id, data$gene_symbol, function(v) length(unique(v[!is.na(v)])))
if (any(multi > 1, na.rm = TRUE))
  log_step("3 consistent", "gene_symbol", sum(multi > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
           paste("symbols shared by >1 MGI ID (kept, flagged):", paste(names(multi)[which(multi > 1)], collapse = ", ")))
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-consistent-gene-symbol
# Examples of noisy symbols before cleaning
head(unique(raw$gene_symbol[grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9.-]", raw$gene_symbol)]), 10)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
Each of the `r length(canon_symbol)` genes now has one symbol; `r n_ref` of them were confirmed by the reference files.
:::

### 6.3 Allele Symbols

The SOP format is `<gene_symbol><allele>`. The part after `<` comes from a small set of real alleles, so each noisy suffix is matched to a valid one with the same letters and digits, and the prefix is replaced by the gene's official symbol.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-allele-symbol
## 3d allele_symbol: <gene_symbol><allele>, brackets closed (SOP)
# The part after '<' comes from a small set of real alleles (tm1b(KOMP)Wtsi ...).
# Each noisy suffix is matched to a valid one by its letters+digits key
# ('tm1b((KOMP)Wts)i>' -> key 'tm1bkompwtsi' -> 'tm1b(KOMP)Wtsi>'),
# and the prefix is replaced by the gene's official symbol.
old <- data$allele_symbol
suffix <- ifelse(!is.na(old) & grepl("<", old), sub("^[^<]*<", "", old), NA)
valid_suffix <- !is.na(suffix) &
  grepl("^(Gt|[a-z]+)[0-9]*[a-z]?(\\.[0-9]+)?(\\([A-Za-z0-9]+\\))?[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*>$", suffix) &
  !grepl("[A-Z]{3,}>$", suffix)                  # All-caps lab code (WTSI) = case noise
key <- tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", suffix))
best_suffix <- tapply(suffix[valid_suffix], key[valid_suffix], mode_of)
fixed_suffix <- ifelse(valid_suffix, suffix, unname(best_suffix[key]))
unrepaired <- !is.na(suffix) & is.na(fixed_suffix)
fixed_suffix[unrepaired] <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9().<>]", "", suffix[unrepaired])
data$allele_symbol <- ifelse(is.na(fixed_suffix) | is.na(data$gene_symbol), NA,
                             paste0(data$gene_symbol, "<", fixed_suffix))
log_step("3 consistent", "allele_symbol", n_changed(old, data$allele_symbol),
         sprintf("prefix set to official gene symbol; %d malformed suffixes repaired from valid alleles",
                 sum(!valid_suffix & !is.na(suffix) & !unrepaired)))
if (any(unrepaired)) log_step("3 consistent", "allele_symbol", sum(unrepaired),
                              "suffix could not be matched; illegal characters stripped only")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r sum(!valid_suffix & !is.na(suffix) & !unrepaired)` malformed allele suffixes were repaired from valid alleles, and `r sum(unrepaired)` could not be matched (illegal characters were removed only).
:::

### 6.4 Strain

`strain_name` must be one of the 9 strains listed in the SOP. Any other value is set to `NA`.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-strain-name
## 3e strain_name: must be one of the 9 SOP strains
bad <- !is.na(data$strain_name) & !(data$strain_name %in% sop_strains)
if (any(bad)) { data$strain_name[bad] <- NA
log_step("3 consistent", "strain_name", sum(bad), "not an SOP strain -> NA") }
log_step("3 consistent", "strain_name", 0, "all values checked against the 9 SOP strains")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r sum(bad)` strain values were not in the SOP list and were set to `NA`.
:::

### 6.5 Life Stage

Values such as `Ear-ly adult` or `E1-2.5` are compared on their letters and digits only, then mapped to the 7 SOP stages, so they are corrected instead of being lost.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-mouse-life-stage
## 3f mouse_life_stage: map noisy text to the 7 SOP stages
# Compare on letters+digits only, so 'Ear-ly adult', 'EARLY ADULT', 'Ea)rly adult'
# and 'E1-2.5' all resolve correctly instead of being lost.
stage_key <- c(e95 = "E9.5", e125 = "E12.5", e155 = "E15.5", e185 = "E18.5",
               earlyadult = "Early adult", middleagedadult = "Middle aged adult",
               lateadult = "Late adult")
old <- data$mouse_life_stage
k <- tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", old))
new <- unname(stage_key[k])
log_step("3 consistent", "mouse_life_stage", n_changed(old, new),
         "case/punctuation/junk characters removed and mapped to the 7 SOP stages")
lost <- !is.na(old) & is.na(new)
if (any(lost)) log_step("3 consistent", "mouse_life_stage", sum(lost),
                        paste("unrecognised -> NA:", paste(head(unique(old[lost]), 5), collapse = "; ")))
data$mouse_life_stage <- factor(new, levels = sop_stages, ordered = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-consistent-mouse-life-stage
# Life stage before cleaning (most common values)
head(sort(table(raw$mouse_life_stage, useNA = "ifany"), decreasing = TRUE), 15)

# Life stage after cleaning
table(data$mouse_life_stage, useNA = "ifany")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
After cleaning, every life stage is one of the 7 SOP values or `NA`. `r sum(lost)` values could not be recognised and were set to `NA`.
:::

### 6.6 Parameter IDs

Junk characters and extra underscores had been added to parameter IDs (for example, `IM_PC_GEL_028_001`). Each ID is rebuilt from its letters and digits in the SOP pattern.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-parameter-id
## 3g parameter_id: PREFIX_PROC_NNN_NNN or PREFIX_NNN_NNN_NNN
# Junk characters AND extra underscores were injected (IM_PC_GEL_028_001,
# M-G-P_014_001_009). The ID is rebuilt from its letters and digits.
rebuild_pid <- function(x) {
  s   <- gsub("[^A-Z0-9]", "", toupper(x))
  out <- rep(NA_character_, length(x))
  a <- !is.na(s) & grepl("^[A-Z]+[A-Z]{3}[0-9]{6}$", s)
  out[a] <- sub("^([A-Z]+)([A-Z]{3})([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})$", "\\1_\\2_\\3_\\4", s[a])
  b <- !is.na(s) & !a & grepl("^[A-Z]+[0-9]{9}$", s)
  out[b] <- sub("^([A-Z]+)([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})([0-9]{3})$", "\\1_\\2_\\3_\\4", s[b])
  out
}
old <- data$parameter_id
data$parameter_id <- rebuild_pid(old)
log_step("3 consistent", "parameter_id", n_changed(old, data$parameter_id),
         "upper case, junk characters and extra underscores removed, ID rebuilt")
lost <- !is.na(old) & is.na(data$parameter_id)
if (any(lost)) log_step("3 consistent", "parameter_id", sum(lost), "could not be rebuilt -> NA")
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r n_changed(old, data$parameter_id)` parameter IDs were rebuilt in the SOP pattern, and `r sum(lost)` could not be rebuilt and were set to `NA`.
:::

### 6.7 Parameter Names

Only an encoding error is fixed here (`NaÃÂ¯ve` becomes `Naïve`). The names are not re-cased, because they must still match the parameter description file used in Step 3.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-parameter-name
## 3h parameter_name: whitespace done; fix a UTF-8 encoding error
old <- data$parameter_name
data$parameter_name <- gsub("Ã\u0083Â¯|Ã¯", "ï", data$parameter_name)
n <- n_changed(old, data$parameter_name)
if (n) log_step("3 consistent", "parameter_name", n, "encoding error fixed ('NaÃÂ¯ve' -> 'Naïve')")
# Names are NOT re-cased: they must match IMPC_parameter_description.txt exactly.
```

### 6.8 Missing Parameter IDs and Names

Each parameter ID has one name. A missing ID is filled from its name only when that name belongs to exactly one ID, and a missing name is filled from its ID. Where there is any doubt, the value stays missing.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-missing-parameter-ids-an
## 3i parameter_id <-> parameter_name: each ID has one name. Fill a missing ID only when
## its name belongs to exactly one ID, and a missing name from its ID.
pairs <- unique(data[!is.na(data$parameter_id) & !is.na(data$parameter_name),
                     c("parameter_id", "parameter_name")])
ids_per_name <- table(pairs$parameter_name)
unique_names <- names(ids_per_name)[ids_per_name == 1]
name_to_id   <- setNames(pairs$parameter_id, pairs$parameter_name)[unique_names]
id_to_name   <- tapply(pairs$parameter_name, pairs$parameter_id, mode_of)

fill <- is.na(data$parameter_id) & data$parameter_name %in% unique_names
data$parameter_id[fill] <- unname(name_to_id[data$parameter_name[fill]])
if (any(fill)) log_step("3 consistent", "parameter_id", sum(fill),
                        "missing ID recovered from a parameter name that maps to exactly one ID")
fill <- is.na(data$parameter_name) & !is.na(data$parameter_id) & data$parameter_id %in% names(id_to_name)
data$parameter_name[fill] <- unname(id_to_name[data$parameter_id[fill]])
if (any(fill)) log_step("3 consistent", "parameter_name", sum(fill), "missing name recovered from parameter ID")
```

### 6.9 LacZ Expression

Each `lacz_*` value is compared on its letters only (so `no express)ion` matches `no expression`) and mapped to one of the 6 values allowed by the SOP.

```{r}
#| label: s02-consistent-lacz
## 3j lacz_*: map to the 6 SOP values
lacz_key <- c(noexpression = "no expression", expression = "expression",
              nodata = "No data", tissuenotavailable = "tissue not available",
              ambiguous = "ambiguous", imageonly = "imageOnly")
for (col in lacz_cols) {
  old <- data[[col]]
  new <- unname(lacz_key[tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z]", "", old))])
  log_step("3 consistent", col, n_changed(old, new), "mapped to the 6 SOP LacZ values")
  lost <- !is.na(old) & is.na(new)
  if (any(lost)) log_step("3 consistent", col, sum(lost), "unrecognised -> NA")
  data[[col]] <- new
}
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
Every `lacz_*` value is now one of the 6 SOP values or `NA`. The malformed values found during exploration, such as `no express)ion` and `no expres%sion`, are corrected to `no expression`.
:::

## 7. Free from Errors

### 7.1 p-values

p-values that are not numbers or lie outside 0–1 are invalid. There is no reliable way to know the correct value, so they are set to `NA` rather than guessed.

```{r}
#| label: s02-free-from-errors-p-values
old <- data$pvalue
p <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(old))
non_num <- !is.na(old) & is.na(p)
if (any(non_num)) log_step("4 error-free", "pvalue", sum(non_num),
                           paste("not a number -> NA:", paste(head(unique(old[non_num]), 5), collapse = "; ")))
out_range <- !is.na(p) & (p < 0 | p > 1)
if (any(out_range)) {
  log_step("4 error-free", "pvalue", sum(out_range),
           paste("outside [0,1] -> NA (invalid, not corrected):", paste(head(p[out_range], 5), collapse = "; ")))
  p[out_range] <- NA
}
data$pvalue <- p
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-free-from-errors-p-values
# Cleaned p-values
summary(data$pvalue)
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Problem found"}
`r sum(non_num)` p-values were not numbers and `r sum(out_range)` were outside 0–1. All of them were set to `NA`.
:::

### 7.2 Text Lengths

The SOP gives a minimum and maximum length for every text field (for example, `gene_symbol` must be 1–13 characters). A value outside these limits is likely to be an error, but the correct value usually cannot be worked out, so these values are **flagged in the log, not changed**.

The check covers the free-text fields only. Fields with a list of allowed values (`strain_name`, `mouse_life_stage` and `lacz_*`) were already checked against that list in section 6, and their SOP length limits contradict the SOP's own allowed values: `tissue not available` has 20 characters (limit 19) and `B6Brd;B6Dnk;B6N-Tyr<c-Brd>` has 26 (limit 25). `analysis_id` is also left out, because its SOP length of 15 is an error (section 6.1).

```{r}
#| label: s02-free-from-errors-text-lengths
# SOP length limits for the text fields
sop <- read.csv("reference_files/IMPC_SOP_2026.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Free-text fields only (fields with an allowed list were checked in section 6)
text_fields <- c("gene_accession_id", "gene_symbol", "parameter_id",
                 "parameter_name", "allele_symbol")
sop_len <- sop[sop$dataField %in% text_fields, c("dataField", "minValue", "maxValue")]

# Count the values in each field that are shorter or longer than the SOP allows
length_check <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(sop_len)), function(i) {
  col <- sop_len$dataField[i]
  x   <- as.character(data[[col]])
  out <- !is.na(x) & (nchar(x) < sop_len$minValue[i] | nchar(x) > sop_len$maxValue[i])
  if (any(out)) log_step("4 error-free", col, sum(out),
                         sprintf("length outside SOP limits (%d-%d characters): flagged, not changed",
                                 as.integer(sop_len$minValue[i]), as.integer(sop_len$maxValue[i])))
  data.frame(column = col, min_length = sop_len$minValue[i], max_length = sop_len$maxValue[i],
             outside_limits = sum(out), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-free-from-errors-text-lengths
# Values outside the SOP length limits, per column
length_check
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r sum(length_check$outside_limits)` values are outside the SOP length limits. Any value outside the limits would be recorded in the log for checking but left unchanged; here, every free-text value is within its limits.
:::

## 8. Unique: Duplicates

Duplicates are removed last, because many duplicate files only match once their noise has been cleaned. Exact copies are removed first; rows that share an analysis ID but differ in content are merged into one row, and any conflicting values are logged.

```{r}
#| label: s02-unique
# Duplicates are removed AFTER cleaning: most duplicate files only differed by
# injected noise, so once cleaned they are identical.
content_cols <- setdiff(names(data), "source_file")
exact <- duplicated(data[content_cols])
if (any(exact)) {
  data <- data[!exact, ]
  log_step("5 unique", "all", sum(exact), "exact duplicate rows removed (after cleaning)")
}

dup_ids <- unique(data$analysis_id[duplicated(data$analysis_id) & !is.na(data$analysis_id)])
if (length(dup_ids)) {
  conflicts <- character(0)
  keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(data))
  for (id in dup_ids) {
    rows  <- which(data$analysis_id == id)
    first <- rows[1]
    for (col in content_cols) {
      vals <- data[[col]][rows]
      vals <- vals[!is.na(vals)]
      if (!length(vals)) next
      if (length(unique(as.character(vals))) > 1) conflicts <- c(conflicts, sprintf("%s:%s", id, col))
      if (is.na(data[[col]][first])) data[[col]][first] <- vals[1]   # Fill gaps from the copy
    }
    keep[rows[-1]] <- FALSE
  }
  data <- data[keep, ]
  log_step("5 unique", "analysis_id", sum(!keep),
           sprintf("same ID, different content: merged into one row (gaps filled from the copy; %d field conflicts kept first value)",
                   length(conflicts)))
  if (length(conflicts)) log_step("5 unique", "analysis_id", length(conflicts),
                                  paste("conflicts:", paste(head(conflicts, 10), collapse = ", ")))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-unique
# Rows before and after
c(raw_rows = nrow(raw), clean_rows = nrow(data))
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r nrow(raw) - nrow(data)` duplicate rows were removed, leaving `r nrow(data)` analyses, each with a unique `analysis_id`.
:::

## 9. Save

The cleaned table and the change log are saved. The remaining `NA` counts in the log include values set to `NA` during cleaning, not only values that were missing in the raw files.

```{r}
#| label: s02-save
na_left <- colSums(is.na(data[content_cols]))
for (col in names(na_left)[na_left > 0])
  log_step("final", col, na_left[[col]], "values still missing (genuinely absent in the source)")
log_step("final", "all", nrow(data),
         sprintf("rows written (%d raw rows in, %d removed as duplicates)", nrow(raw), nrow(raw) - nrow(data)))

data$mouse_life_stage <- as.character(data$mouse_life_stage)
write.csv(data, out_file, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
write.csv(change_log, log_file, row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

message(sprintf("\nWrote %s (%d rows x %d columns) and %s (%d steps)",
                out_file, nrow(data), ncol(data), log_file, nrow(change_log)))
```

```{r}
#| label: s02-view-save
# Full change log
change_log
```

::: {.callout-note title="Finding"}
`r sum(trimws(raw$gene_symbol) %in% na_tokens)` gene symbols were missing in the raw data, and `r sum(is.na(data$gene_symbol))` are missing after cleaning: every analysis now has a gene symbol, recovered from its MGI ID (section 6.2). The values that are still missing (for example `r sum(is.na(data$pvalue))` p-values and `r sum(is.na(data$parameter_id))` parameter IDs) could not be worked out from the data or a reference file, so they are kept as `NA`.
:::

## 10. Reproducibility Record

The MD5 hash acts as a fingerprint of each output file: if the script is run again on the same input and produces the same hashes, the outputs are identical. The R session details are recorded so the same package versions can be used again.

```{r}
#| label: s02-reproducibility-record
tools::md5sum(c("cleaned_data.csv", "cleaned_data_log.csv"))
sessionInfo()
```

## 11. Summary and Next Step

Every value in the table now follows the SOP or is `NA`, and every analysis appears once. All changes, with the number of rows affected, are recorded in `cleaned_data_log.csv`.

::: {.callout-tip title="Next step"}
In Step 3 (`03_metadata_cleaning`), the supporting files (procedures, parameters, disease information, homology and the query genes) are cleaned and turned into normalised database tables. `cleaned_data.csv` is used there to link those tables to the analyses.
:::
